image_description: An underwater scene featuring a hammerhead shark swimming near the surface, illuminated by sunlight filtering through the water. The shark is viewed from below and the side, showing its distinctive head shape, dorsal fin, pectoral fins, and tail. Other smaller fish are visible in the background, along with rocky structures at the bottom left.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The shark clearly displays the iconic T-shaped head structure characteristic of hammerheads.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Dark spots corresponding to eyes are visible at the outermost edges of the hammer-shaped head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The resolution and angle of the image do not allow for the clear identification of nostrils on the underside or margin of the cephalofoil.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front edge of the head appears consistent with the description, showing a slight curve/indentation typical of the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is elongated and thin from the side view, matching the streamlined description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The top of the shark is darker (greyish) while the belly area is visibly lighter/white, consistent with countershading.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in dermal denticles with a rough texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Image resolution is insufficient to resolve microscopic skin textures like dermal denticles.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate (sickle-shaped), positioned anteriorly.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A prominent, curved dorsal fin is visible on the back of the shark.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The side fins are visible and match the broad, triangular morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail fin clearly shows a larger upper lobe compared to the lower lobe, typical of pelagic sharks.
